# A Holiday for the Holidays · Ohio's Gas Tax Holiday · DNSC

> What you pay, what the state pays, and why gas costs this much: Ohio's 90-day gas tax holiday followed from your pump back to the price of a barrel.

Ohio's Gas Tax Holiday · From the pump to the price of oil

Oct 4, 2026 to Jan 2, 2027 · H.B. 519 · Gasoline and diesel

Free, from the public record

## A holiday for the holidays.

Ohio took its 38.5¢ gas tax off every gallon for 90 days. Start with your own tank, then follow the oil from your pump to the price of a barrel.

1 · Your pump

Gold is what you pay. Teal is what Ohio's general fund now covers for you.

[Chart: A fuel tank, filled to your tank size]

### How big is your tank?

15 gallons

A choice (Fuel): Gas, Diesel.

A slider sets Tank size in gallons from 5 to 40, starting at 15.

A text field: What a gallon really costs, starting at $4.26.

A slider sets Price per gallon, tax included from 2.5 to 8, starting at 4.26.

A slider sets Fill-ups per week from 0.5 to 5, starting at 1.

This fill-up really costs

You pay

Ohio pays

**For your business: vehicles, gallons, savings**

### For your business

A slider sets Number of vehicles from 1 to 200, starting at 10.

A slider sets Gallons per vehicle per week from 5 to 600, starting at 60.

A choice (Fleet fuel): Gas, Diesel.

Gallons in 90 days

Every week

All 90 days

Trucks that cross state lines pay Ohio's fuel use tax on the miles they drive in Ohio. The holiday cuts that tax too, so the savings follow Ohio miles wherever the tank was filled.

**Sources for this part**

- Ohio Legislative Service Commission, [Bill Analysis, H.B. 519](https://www.legislature.ohio.gov/download?key=28854) (rates: 38.5¢ gas, 47¢ diesel, to 0.01¢).
- Ohio Department of Taxation, [Motor Fuel Tax](https://tax.ohio.gov/business/motor-fuel-tax): "From 10/4/2026-1/2/2027 the rate for gas and diesel is reduced to $0.0001."
- U.S. Energy Information Administration, weekly [Ohio regular gasoline](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMM_EPMR_PTE_SOH_DPG&f=W) and [Midwest diesel](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG&f=W) prices (the default prices).
- Method: savings per gallon are the old rate minus the holiday rate (38.49¢ gas, 46.99¢ diesel); each fill-up assumes a full tank; a weekly habit repeats 90 ÷ 7 ≈ 12.9 times.

2 · The holiday

### Ninety days, October 4 to January 2.

Right through the holidays. Here's how it works at the station.

Swipe the calendar →

**Day 1** of 90. 89 to go, through January 2.

[Chart: Calendar from October 4, 2026 to January 2, 2027 with Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's marked]

[Chart: A line drawing of a gas station]

- **The full cut, from day one.** Stations must pass the whole 38.5¢ to buyers.
- **They get back tax they already paid.** Fuel already in the ground tanks was taxed. Stations claim it by March 1.
- **Leftover tax-free fuel pays up later.** Fuel bought tax-free but sold after January 2 owes the tax, also by March 1.
- **The pump sticker can stay.** No new tax stickers required. Stations may update the rate on them.
- **Keep the cut, and the state can act.** It counts against the station's license and as a deceptive sales practice. The Attorney General enforces it.

**The details: what the bill says, word for word in plain English**

**The rate.** Ohio's tax drops from 38.5¢ to 0.01¢ a gallon on gas, and from 47¢ to 0.01¢ on diesel. It also cuts the fuel use tax commercial trucks pay on Ohio miles. Natural gas, propane and LNG are not affected.

**Who pays the tax normally.** The motor fuel tax is levied on fuel dealers (wholesalers, refineries and importers), and the cost is generally passed down to gas stations and then to buyers.

**Refunds.** For fuel already taxed at the old rate and sold during the holiday, stations apply to the Tax Commissioner by March 1, 2027, and are paid within 30 days from the Tax Refund Fund.

**Leftovers.** Fuel bought at the holiday rate and sold after it ends owes the difference, due March 1, 2027. A station can file both on one form so they net out.

**Stickers.** The state doesn't have to print new pump tax stickers. Stations may change the posted rate on them, as long as they don't damage the sticker.

**Enforcement.** Selling without passing on the full cut may count in the Tax Commissioner's licensing decisions and is an unfair or deceptive act under the Consumer Sales Practices Act. Only the Attorney General can enforce it; buyers can't sue on their own under this rule.

**Paperwork.** The Tax Department may delay its December distribution up to ten business days. October's report deadline moves from Nov 30 to Dec 7–15, 2026.

**How it passed.** H.B. 519 began as a car-theft bill. On Sept 30, 2026 the Senate added the holiday and passed it 26 to 5; the House agreed 78 to 16 the same day. Gov. DeWine signed it Oct 1. The federal 18.4¢ gas and 24.4¢ diesel taxes still apply.

- Ohio Legislative Service Commission, [Bill Analysis, H.B. 519](https://www.legislature.ohio.gov/download?key=28854), Sept 30, 2026.
- Ohio General Assembly, [H.B. 519 status](https://www.legislature.ohio.gov/legislation/136/hb519/status).
- U.S. Energy Information Administration, [federal fuel taxes](https://www.eia.gov/tools/faqs/faq.php?id=10&t=10).

3 · The statehouse

### $725 million from the state's own fund covers the road money.

Fuel tax pays for roads and bridges. The state set aside money from its general fund, so ODOT, cities, counties and townships still get paid, on the months the tax would have arrived.

Swipe the chart →

[Chart: Money flows from the Ohio Statehouse to road budgets between December and February]

Set aside by the bill

$725M

From the General Revenue Fund, the state's main operating account.

Estimated tax not collected

$698M

The budget office's estimate for the 90 days.

Left in the general fund, June 30

$2.43B

Ohio took in $1.82B more in taxes than its budget expected last year.

**Ohio's surplus, in scale**

The general fund's money left over at year end, after bills already promised, was $2.43 billion. The rainy day fund held another $3.99 billion on June 30; spending it takes a vote of the legislature, and the holiday doesn't touch it. The $725 million is about 30% of the general fund's leftover. Counting everything, general fund revenue came in $981 million above the estimate.

**Every recipient, and your own share**

| Recipient | Estimated share of the $698.0M, 90 days |
|---|---|
| Ohio Department of Transportation | $373.6M |
| Highway debt payments | $73.1M |
| Ohio Public Works Commission | $16.8M |
| Ohio Department of Natural Resources | $6.7M |
| Ohio Department of Taxation | $1.5M |
| Turnpike Commission | $0.7M |
| Public Utilities Commission | $0.3M |
| Local governments | $225.3M |
| Municipalities (part of local governments) | $94.7M |
| Counties (part of local governments) | $81.6M |
| Townships (part of local governments) | $49.0M |
| Total | $698.0M |

"Your share" splits the state-paid part of your 90 days in the same proportions. About 65% of the first 28¢ of the tax goes to the state for transportation and the rest to local governments; of the part above 28¢, added in 2019, 55% goes to the state and 45% to locals. Spread across 88 counties, the counties' share averages about $927,000 each. The set-aside is $27 million more than the estimate; a separate $250,000 runs the holiday. Fuel tax reaches recipients about two months after the gas is bought, so a holiday from October to early January lands in road budgets from December through February.

**Sources for this part**

- Ohio Legislative Budget Office, [Fiscal Note, H.B. 519](https://www.legislature.ohio.gov/download?key=28857) ($725M item 110413 "Tax Relief Hold Harmless," $250K item 110414, $698M estimate, allocation table, timing).
- Ohio Legislative Service Commission, [Bill Analysis, H.B. 519](https://www.legislature.ohio.gov/download?key=28854) (the 65% and 55% splits).
- Ohio Legislative Budget Office, [Budget Footnotes, July 2026](https://www.lsc.ohio.gov/assets/organizations/legislative-service-commission/files/fy-2026-budget-footnotes-july-2026.pdf) and [Budget Stabilization Fund, July 2026](https://www.lsc.ohio.gov/assets/organizations/legislative-service-commission/files/infographics-budget-stabilization-fund-july-2026.pdf).

4 · The refinery

### Ohio refines oil from Canada and the Midwest.

Four refineries turn crude into the gas in your tank. Almost all of it arrives by pipeline.

Swipe the map →

[Chart: Map of Ohio with its four refineries and the main pipelines coming in]

Refinery · Pipeline route, simplified · Utica shale counties

**4 refineries** Lima, two near Toledo, and Canton.

**607,000 barrels a day** About 3% of the nation's refining.

**98% by pipeline** From Canada through Michigan, and up from Texas on the Mid-Valley line.

**0 from the Persian Gulf** Every barrel the Midwest imported in 2025 came from Canada. None from the Gulf since 2018.

What's in a gallon, U.S. average, May 2026

Gas$4.48

Crude oil 52% · Refining 22% · Selling 15% · Taxes 12%

Diesel$5.60

Crude oil 42% · Refining 25% · Selling 23% · Taxes 11%

**The refineries, and where the crude comes from**

| Refinery | Owner | Barrels a day |
|---|---|---|
| Lima | Cenovus | 183,000 |
| Toledo | PBF Energy | 172,800 |
| Oregon, near Toledo | Cenovus | 150,800 |
| Canton | Marathon | 100,000 |

EIA lists Ohio's crude sources as Canada, the Midcontinent, North Dakota, the Appalachian Basin, the Gulf Coast and Ohio's own Utica shale. Selling means distribution and marketing; taxes are federal and state together. Because the tax is a set amount per gallon, its share shrinks as prices rise: in 2025, at $3.10 a gallon, taxes were 14% of gas. Pipeline routes on the map are simplified.

- EIA, [Refinery Capacity Report](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/refinerycapacity/), as of Jan 1, 2026.
- EIA, [Ohio State Energy Profile](https://www.eia.gov/states/OH/analysis).
- EIA, [Midwest crude imports by country](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/pet_move_impcp_d_r20_Z00_mbblpd_a.htm), [imports from the Persian Gulf](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=MCRIPP2PG2&f=A), and [refinery receipts by method](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/pet_pnp_caprec_dcu_r20_a.htm), 2025.
- Energy Transfer, [Mid-Valley Pipeline tariff](https://commoncarrier.energytransfer.com/InfoPost/CommonCarriers/resources/MVPL/Tariffs/MVPL_FERC_483.23.0.pdf); Enbridge, [Stockbridge Terminal](https://www.enbridge.com/~/media/Enb/Documents/Factsheets/FS_ENB_Stockbridge_Terminal.pdf).
- EIA, [Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/), "What we pay for in a gallon," May 2026; [Factors affecting gasoline prices](https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/gasoline/factors-affecting-gasoline-prices.php).

5 · The auction

"Oil markets are essentially a global auction. The highest bidder will win the available supply."

*U.S. Energy Information Administration*

A choice (Show the world now or if the war ends): Now, What if the war ends?

Swipe the map →

[Chart: World map of the oil flows in the story]

Canada and the U.S. to Ohio · Venezuela · Russia · Persian Gulf, about half blocked · Buyers bidding · Routes simplified

**Every refinery bids for the same barrels.** Oil sells on one world market, so a shortage anywhere raises the price everywhere, including Ohio.

**A fifth of the world's oil went through Hormuz.** About 20 million barrels a day in 2024. Since Feb 28, about half of that has stopped.

**Venezuela's oil changed course.** After the U.S. lifted most sanctions in January, Venezuelan crude to the U.S. rose from 137,000 barrels a day to 701,000 by July, almost all of it to the Gulf Coast. Ohio refines none of it.

**The Americas pumped more.** The U.S., Canada, Brazil, Guyana and Argentina add about 1.4 million barrels a day this year, far short of what's missing from the Gulf.

**Canada sells Ohio its oil, through a tense year.** The U.S. put a 10% tariff on Canadian energy in March 2025. Even so, 90% of Canada's crude exports still came to the U.S. in 2025, and Line 5 keeps feeding Toledo's refineries.

**Russia's oil found new buyers.** After U.S. sanctions in October 2025 and the Hormuz shutdown, India bought a record 2.6 million barrels a day of Russian crude in July.

No one can promise a price. Here is what the record and the forecasters show.

Before the war, about 20 million barrels a day moved through Hormuz. By May it was under 10. If the war ends, it won't snap back overnight: the IEA says "a full recovery will not be immediate," because mines must be cleared and supply chains rebuilt, and it expects most of the rebound in 2027.

It happened once already · −52¢

In the three weeks after the mid-June deal to reopen the strait, Ohio's price fell 52¢, to **$3.56** on July 6. Prices had been easing since May on reports of a deal. The relief lasted about three weeks.

Same agency, two forecasts · 57¢ apart

In July, with the strait open, the federal EIA expected Midwest gas to average **$3.17** this October to December. In September, assuming the strait stays constrained through year end, it expected **$3.74**. Two forecasts under different conditions.

How fast it reaches the pump · 2.4¢

Each $1 change in a barrel of crude moves gas about 2.4¢ a gallon. About half shows up within two weeks and 80% within four. Pump prices fall more slowly than crude does.

How big is 38.5¢?

The gas tax holiday

**38.5¢**

Ohio, three weeks after the June deal

**52¢**

Between EIA's July and September forecasts

**57¢**

**Sources for this part**

- EIA, [Oil prices and outlook](https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/oil-and-petroleum-products/prices-and-outlook.php) (the "global auction" line).

- IEA, [Oil Market Report, September 2026](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-september-2026): the U.S., Canada, Brazil, Guyana and Argentina add 1.4 mb/d in 2026.
- EIA, [weekly Brent spot price](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=RBRTE&f=W) (about $71 before the war; weekly highs above $120).
- Map arcs show the flows in this story, simplified; they are not shipping routes.

- Canada Energy Regulator, [Overview of 2025 Canada–U.S. energy trade](https://www.cer-rec.gc.ca/en/data-analysis/energy-markets/market-snapshots/2026/market-snapshot-overview-of-2025-canada-us-energy-trade.html), May 27, 2026 (90.1% of crude exports to the U.S.; Trans Mountain).
- Michigan Attorney General, [Line 5 ruling](https://www.michigan.gov/ag/news/press-releases/2026/04/22/us-supreme-court-unanimously-rules-ag-nessels-line-5-lawsuit), Apr 22, 2026.
- gCaptain, [Treasury sanctions Rosneft and Lukoil](https://gcaptain.com/u-s-treasury-sanctions-russias-largest-oil-companies-over-ukraine/), Oct 2025, and [waiver for stranded Russian cargoes](https://gcaptain.com/treasury-extends-russian-oil-waiver-as-hormuz-crisis-tightens-global-supplies/), 2026.
- KSE Institute, [Russian Oil Tracker, August 2026](https://institute.kse.ua/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/rot_eng_august_2026.pdf) (India 2.6 mb/d in July; product exports at a record low); CREA, [August 2026 analysis](https://energyandcleanair.org/august-2026-monthly-analysis-of-russian-fossil-fuel-exports-and-sanctions/) (port strikes).
- IEA, [Oil Market Report, June 2026](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-june-2026) ("a full recovery will not be immediate"; Hormuz flow fell to 9.6 mb/d in May) and [September 2026](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-september-2026) (recovery deferred to 2027).
- EIA, Short-Term Energy Outlook, [July 2026](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/jul26.pdf) (Midwest regular $3.17 for Oct to Dec with the strait open; "retail prices historically decrease more slowly than crude oil prices") and [September 2026](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/sep26.pdf) ($3.74 with the strait constrained through year end).
- EIA, [Today in Energy, June 26, 2012](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=6850): each $1 a barrel moves gasoline about 2.4¢ a gallon; about half within two weeks and 80% within four.
- EIA, [Today in Energy, Apr 7, 2026](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67424) (the Feb 28 strikes and the strait's "de facto closure") and [July 15, 2026](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67865) (the June deal, the late-June low, the renewed blockade).

6 · The barrel

### The barrel sets the price.

Brent crude, the world's benchmark, the week before the war and the latest week. The holiday moves the pump 38.5¢; the barrel moves everything else.

### The price of a barrel

Brent crude, weekly, EIA

Before the war, week of Feb 27

$71

a barrel of Brent crude.

Latest, week of Sep 25

$117

a barrel. Up 64% since the war began.

**Why prices are this high.** Since the Iran war began on February 28, about half the tankers through the Strait of Hormuz have stopped. Ohio's gas followed the barrel, from $2.89 to a peak of $4.78 in May. The holiday takes 38.5¢ off the price; the rest follows the world oil market.

**Oil and pump prices, week by week, since 2020**

A deal in mid-June reopened the strait for a few weeks; it frayed in July, and the U.S. blockade of Iranian oil returned. Beyond crude, a gallon carries refining and retail costs and the 18.4¢ federal tax.

A choice (Time range): Since 2020, 2026.

Ohio · U.S. average · Brent crude oil · Iran war, from Feb 28, 2026

[Chart: Weekly Brent crude oil price and Ohio and U.S. regular gasoline prices since 2020]

Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration: weekly Brent crude spot price, and weekly retail regular gasoline for Ohio and the U.S. Gas prices are released every Monday. # The table

> What six companies and a President signed on September 29, 2026: the page in their words, the faces and what each one said after, what it binds, what it doesn't, and what would.

DNSC · From the public record

The table · October 4, 2026 · Understanding the week, from the record

From the record, Sept. 29 to Oct. 4

## They promised to check themselves.

The President and six AI companies signed a one-page accord on superintelligence over lunch on September 29.

Published October 4, 2026

Related · At the Department of War, September 30: [the task force](https://tools.dnsc.ai/civic/task-force/).

[Image: The East Room of the White House set for lunch, guests along a long table, the press at the far end.]

I think it's morally binding, yeah.

**Donald J. Trump**, President of the United States · asked whether the accord is binding in any way · 0:57 into the press availability [19]

The East Room, September 29, 2026 · Official White House photo by Daniel Torok · public domain

Who was at the table

### Eight companies at the table. Six signed.

Outside the West Wing lobby · after lunch · 33 minutes at the microphones

What they said, after

### Nine people took the microphones. [19]

[Image: The President at the lunch table, mid-sentence, hand raised.]

At the lunch table, East Room.Official White House photo by Daniel Torok · public domain · cropped

#### The head of the tableWhat Donald J. Trump said

We're also thinking about forming a committee of sorts where we put maybe 10 people on that committee. It could be from that group.

**Donald J. Trump**, President of the United States · 2:22

The committee is in the future tense and is not in the accord. As of October 4 there is no committee, no calendar and no czar.

**More from Donald J. Trump, President of the United States**

"Why not convene this group on a quarterly basis, on a yearly basis?" "Well, did I say we wouldn't?"

14:12, 14:18

"I'll be naming, I'd say over the next three or four days. I wanna check with the companies."

16:29, on a czar · none named as of Oct. 4

"We have the smartest people in the world watching over each other."

10:57

"Who would hold you accountable?" "Because they're outstanding people and they don't want anybody, they don't want anything to go wrong." "Their companies are at stake, if something goes wrong."

23:59, 24:00, 24:09 · the question was put to the executives; the President answered

"Mr. President, how do you enforce the policing?" "He's a good man, he's right here." "It's a good idea." "Thank you everybody."

31:23 to 31:40 · the last question on the accord

Cross-talk throughout: "Mr. President. Mr. President." At 20:53 a follow-up on self-policing is stopped with "hold it, hold it, hold. CNN fake news."

**What he holds**President of the United States. Net worth $7 billion, as estimated by Forbes, Oct. 4, 2026. [26] · Controls the Trump Organization through a trust, and 114,750,000 shares of Trump Media & Technology Group, 41.5 percent of the company, held in a revocable trust of which he is the sole beneficiary and his son the sole trustee. [37] · Public financial disclosure on file: OGE Form 278e for 2025, filed June 2026, 927 pages. [38]

[Image: Speaker Mike Johnson seated at the lunch table, smiling.]

Across from the President, East Room.Official White House photo by Daniel Torok · public domain · cropped

#### The other seat at the headWhat Mike Johnson said

Trust is earned. It's not automatic.

**Mike Johnson**, Speaker of the House · 10:07

The room, by the numbers

### What was sitting at one table.

The companies at the table

**$15.6 trillion** the six companies that signed, xAI counted as SpaceX

**$23.6 trillion** the whole table, signers and not

**How the companies are counted**

Public companies at CompaniesMarketCap's close-of-day figures for Oct. 3, 2026. xAI is counted as SpaceX, which absorbed it in February 2026 and has traded on Nasdaq as SPCX since June 12, 2026. Private companies at their last reported rounds: Anthropic $965 billion (May 2026), OpenAI $852 billion (March 2026; reported in talks at $1.4 trillion on Sept. 29). The two kinds of number are not the same thing and are added here only to size the room. [27][28][29][30][41]

The people at the microphones

**$1.48 trillion** the seven with a published estimate, together

**How the people are counted**

As estimated by Forbes on Oct. 4, 2026; the Speaker and Mr. Sankar have no estimate from Forbes or Bloomberg. [26]

Ten companies sat at one table. Three of them run the clouds that took 63 percent of the world's spending on cloud infrastructure in the second quarter of this year: Amazon 28 percent, Microsoft 20, Google 15. [40] The page they signed asks each of these companies to check itself.

What they actually signed

### One page of text. One page of signatures. Written in "should."

[Image: Page one of the accord: the title, the preamble, the four numbered layers, and three closing paragraphs.][Image: Page two of the accord: the President's signature at left and six company signatures at right.]

Both pages, as the President posted them that evening. Under his signature the title reads "President of the Unites States."Posted by the President on Truth Social, Sept. 29, 2026, 5:24 PM · a government document from the public record [18]

We believe every company is responsible for developing its own technology safely.

The first sentence is the whole theory of governance: each company keeps its own checks. [2]

Four checks, all inside each company · What each one means, and what it does not bind. [2]

1. Internal controls **What it means**The company watches its own models. **What it doesn't bind**Which controls, how strong, or by when.
2. An internal team **What it means**The company's own staff check that the controls work. **What it doesn't bind**Anyone outside the company sees what they find.
3. An independent external auditor **What it means**Someone from outside assesses the controls. **What it doesn't bind**Who the auditor is. The company chooses, pays, and need not publish the result.
4. A committee of the board **What it means**The company's own directors receive the reports and see that issues are fixed. **What it doesn't bind**Any regulator, legislature or member of the public.

Nothing in the page connects one company's four to another's. [2]

The participating companies will meet regularly to establish standards and best practices. No date, no chair, no minutes.

Over time, it may make sense to codify these steps into laws or regulations. It does not say when, or who writes them.

**The four layers, in the page's words**

"Implement robust internal controls to monitor the capabilities and alignment of its models during training and deployment around areas like cybersecurity, biosecurity, and chemical threats, and to ensure that its models do not hack or access technical systems in unintended ways."

Layer 1 · inside the company

"Empower an internal team to ensure all of the controls, monitoring, and detection are operating as intended, and that any issues are remediated."

Layer 2 · inside the company

"Partner with an independent external auditor or evaluator to carry out independent assessments of whether the controls, monitoring, and detection are operating as intended."

Layer 3 · chosen by the company

"Designate an independent committee of the board of directors to oversee and receive reports from the teams operating the controls and the internal and external auditors and evaluators, as well as to ensure any issues identified are remediated."

Layer 4 · the company's own board

**What the page leaves out**

**No standard.** Layer one names no control, strength or deadline. **Nothing has to be reported outside.** Layer two's team reports to the company. **No one else picks the auditor, and nothing has to be published.** Layer three lets each company choose its own assessor; no result has to go to any government body. **No one outside reads the report.** Layer four ends at a board that answers to shareholders. **No force.** The page uses "should" for the companies and "believe" for the signers; it sets no deadline, names no penalty and requires no incident to be reported to anyone outside the company. [2][3][5]

How it would be governed

### Who schedules the meetings?

- Who schedules, and how often? Unknown"Will meet regularly." No date, no convener. [2]
- Who arbitrates between two signers? UnknownNo chair, no vote named. [2][5]
- Who audits, and who picks them? RecordAn outside auditor, chosen by the company being audited. [2][3]
- What gets reported, to whom? RecordTo the company's own board. Nothing to any government body; nothing published. [3][5]
- What department is this? UnknownA "10-person committee" and a czar were promised at the microphones. Neither exists as of Oct. 4. [19]
- What did the government commit to? RecordIts signature, and an order renaming AI to SI across federal usage, with a definition due in 60 days. No office, no duty. [6][8]

What right does this have

### None in law. It was signed the same afternoon the Senate was asked to pass one.

What binds, and what would · Each row says what the instrument reaches that the accord does not. [5]

| Instrument | What it binds that the accord doesn't | Status, Oct. 4, 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| **The accord** Sept. 29, 2026 · voluntary | Nothing beyond what each signer chooses. | Signed by six and the President. "Should." No penalty, no reporting. |
| **Executive order, "Era of Super Intelligence"** Sept. 29, 2026 | Federal vocabulary. "SI." A definition due in 60 days. | In force. Binds words, not conduct. [8] |
| **California SB 53** In force Jan. 1, 2026 | Published safety frameworks; incidents reported to the state in 15 days, or 24 hours when danger is imminent; whistleblowers protected. | In force; already covers the model builders at the table. Up to $1 million per violation. [9] |
| **New York RAISE Act** Compliance Jan. 2027 | State registration from November 2026; incidents reported within 72 hours; quarterly risk assessments. | Registration opens next month. [10] |
| **AI Risk Management and Security Act** Warner, Schatz, Kim · Senate | A federal safety board with access to new models 45 days before release. | Blocked on the floor Sept. 29, the afternoon of the accord, by Sen. Cruz's objection. relayed [11] |
| **AI Risk Evaluation Act** Hawley, Blumenthal · Sept. 2025 | Pre-deployment testing at the Energy Department, with penalties. | Introduced; no floor action. Blumenthal, Oct. 1: the accord "seems to give Congress a free pass." [12][13] |
| **AI Agent Accountability Act** Murphy, Hawley · Oct. 1, 2026 | Criminal and civil liability for agents that cause hacking damage. | Announced two days after the accord. [14] |
| **Great American AI Act** House draft · June 4, 2026 | Transparency and independent audits for large developers; three-year preemption of state development laws. | Still a draft. [16] |
| **EO 14365 and the state-law fight** Dec. 11, 2025 | A Justice Department task force to sue states; the ten-year moratorium lost 99 to 1. | Task force in place; 29 states enacted AI laws in H1 2026. [17] |

**Is the accord being used as an argument against the bills?**

No official has cited it by name as a reason to stop a bill. The Vice President, Sept. 29: "The solution to some of the AI risks is for you guys to take the risk seriously, not to come to the government for a regulatory regime." The Senate Majority Leader said Congress will need to legislate "at some point." The one bill that reached the floor that day was blocked the same afternoon. [4][11] What the table shows: the only instruments that bind the companies at the table today are two state laws.

The last question on the accord · 31:23

### Mr. President, how do you enforce the policing?

He's a good man, he's right here. It's a good idea. Thank you everybody.

**The President** · 31:30, 31:32 and 31:40 · a shouted question on campaign ads came between the last two [19]

That is the state of enforcement on October 4: a good idea.

# The task force

> On September 30, 2026 the Secretary of War named Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey and Newt Gingrich to co-direct a 120-day study of future war. Who they are, what they build, what they hold and sell to the Department, what it means for Ohio, and what the study can and cannot decide.

DNSC · From the public record

The task force · October 4, 2026 · Understanding the week, from the record

From the record · Sept. 30 to Oct. 4

## Three men in the balcony. One hundred and twenty days.

On September 30 the Secretary of War asked Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey and Newt Gingrich to tell the Department what the next war will need, and announced a new command for drones. Two of the three sell to the Department.

Published October 4, 2026

[Image: Palmer Luckey, Newt Gingrich and Elon Musk standing at a balcony rail in the auditorium at Quantico, the audience below them applauding.]

From left, Palmer Luckey, Newt Gingrich and Elon Musk stand during the Secretary's remarks, Quantico, Va., September 30, 2026.Official DoW photo by Navy Petty Officer 1st Class Eric Brann · public domain · cropped [4]

Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey, and Newt Gingrich, all of whom are up in the audience with us today.

**Pete Hegseth, Secretary of War** · naming the co-directors of Project Meridian · about 30:36 [3]

What the Secretary announced

### A command and a study.

At Marine Corps Base Quantico, the Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, gave a "State of the Force" address to about 600 junior officers and enlisted leaders and announced six initiatives, each with a signed memo. These two carry the three names. [1][5][6]

1 · A command

> AUTOWARCOM, the Autonomous Warfare Command: a four-star command for drones and autonomous systems, with its own manpower, budget, acquisition authorities.

RecordTarget date October 1, 2027. Needs CongressThe memo says it must secure necessary legislation. No budget, no commander named. [5][6]

**The command, in more detail**

The memo: it will define joint needs and integrate Service-provided forces in support of geographic combatant commanders. A functional command, like Special Operations or Cyber, both of which Congress created by law. A Senate committee bill already proposes one like it, voted 18 to 9 on June 11, 2026. [5][33]

Until then, the drone program office becomes Project Agincourt, run by Owen West of the Defense Innovation Unit and Navy SEAL Senior Chief Max Strasiser, reporting to the Secretary monthly. Document: "Project Agincourt - Pathway to the Autonomous Warfare Command," Sept. 30, 2026. [5][6]

Drone warfare supercharged by SI-enabled targeting is the biggest battlefield revolution in generations.

Hegseth, about 21:56 [3]

2 · A study

> Project Meridian: a study of future war, due in 120 days, January 28, 2027, as an unclassified, publicly released final report with a classified annex.

RecordDirected by Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey and Newt Gingrich; led by MITRE for the Department's technology officer. [5][6][7]

**The study, in more detail**

The memo names one person: Effective immediately, I am directing the DoW's Chief Technology Officer, Emil Michael, to commission Project Meridian: The Future of Warfare, through a partner organization. The release names the three co-directors. MITRE named itself on October 2 and listed 17 more participants. Document: "Commissioning of Project Meridian: The Future of Warfare," Sept. 30, 2026. [5][6][7]

The speech, the release and the memo agree on 120 days. The day before, the President signed an order renaming AI "Super Intelligence" across the executive branch, and six companies signed a voluntary accord at lunch, Musk for xAI. [3][31]

The three co-directors

### A rocket maker, a weapons maker, a former Speaker.

What each builds, what each holds, what each sells to the Department, and what each has said, in his own words.

[Image: Elon Musk at the balcony rail at Quantico.]

Quantico, Sept. 30 · official DoW photo, cropped [4]

#### Co-director · SpaceX, Tesla, xAI Elon Musk

Rockets and satellites at SpaceX, cars and a humanoid robot at Tesla, and the AI company xAI, merged into SpaceX in February 2026. The day before Quantico, he signed the White House accord for xAI. [13][31]

I don't feel comfortable building that robot army if I don't have at least a strong influence.

**Elon Musk** · Tesla earnings call, Oct. 22, 2025, on his voting control · relayed by transcript [10]

**What he holds**Tesla: 19.9 percent, per his Schedule 13G/A, event date June 16, 2026. SpaceX: 48.4 percent of the Class A common stock as his Schedule 13G counts it, with his Class B shares and options converted, event date June 30, 2026. Net worth $981 billion, Forbes, Oct. 4, 2026. [13][15]

**What he sells to the Department**SpaceX: national security launches, anticipated value $5,923,580,297, awarded by the Space Force Apr. 4, 2025. A $1.8 billion contract with the National Reconnaissance Office for a spy satellite network, signed 2021, reported by Reuters in 2024. [16][17]

**More in his words**

I, I think by far the most likely outcome is an age of abundance, uh, where we don't have just a universal basic income, we have universal high income.

Outside the West Wing after the lunch, Sept. 29, about 29:26 [9]

when you have, uh, robots and you have super intelligence, it means that everyone in the world can have better medical care than anyone here, including me.

Same, about 29:38 [9]

He said nothing about the military at the lunch or the gaggle, and he has not spoken publicly about Meridian since September 30. He did not answer Politico's questions. [8][9]

[Image: Palmer Luckey at the balcony rail at Quantico, in a floral shirt and dark blazer.]

Quantico, Sept. 30 · official DoW photo, cropped [4]

#### Co-director · founder of Anduril Palmer Luckey

Anduril, in its own words: advanced autonomous systems and defense technology to protect US and allied forces. Drones, interceptors, an autonomous fighter, and the software that links them. Its 5 million square foot plant is in Ohio. [20][26]

How stupid would I feel if I won a bunch of contracts to build the things that would deter China from invading Taiwan, and then, because it takes three years to get them out the door, the war happens?

**Palmer Luckey** · on building fast in Ohio · relayed by Axios, Mar. 18, 2026 [18]

**What he holds**Founder of Anduril Industries (2017), valued at $61 billion in a May 2026 round. His stake is not public. Net worth $6 billion, Forbes, Oct. 4, 2026. [21]

**What he sells to the Department**An Army enterprise contract worth up to $20 billion over ten years, from Mar. 12, 2026. In June 2026 the Air Force selected Anduril's autonomous fighter, the FQ-44 Fury, for production; the value was not disclosed. [22][29]

**More in his words**

There's no moral high ground to making a land mine that kills indiscriminately.

At a TED talk Q&A, relayed by TechRadar, Aug. 5, 2026 [19]

We're ahead of schedule

On the Ohio plant, relayed by Axios, Mar. 18, 2026 [18]

He has not spoken publicly about Meridian since September 30. His company told Politico it would commit to complying with highest ethical standards where actual conflicts of interest arise. [8]

[Image: Newt Gingrich at the balcony rail at Quantico.]

Quantico, Sept. 30 · official DoW photo, cropped [4]

#### Co-director · former Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich

Speaker from 1995 to 1999. Chairman of Gingrich 360, a Fox News contributor. Named to the Defense Policy Board in December 2020 and removed in February 2021. [24][25]

It's an honor to be serving as codirector for Project Meridian. This is critical work that will secure the future of America and keep us free, prosperous, and safe for a generation.

**Newt Gingrich** · on X, Sept. 30, 2026 [23]

**What he holds**Chairman, Gingrich 360. No published net worth estimate. No contracts with the Department found. [24]

**More in his words**

It's a very big challenge

On Fox Business, relayed by Gingrich 360, Oct. 2, 2026. His company describes the job as looking "25 to 30 years into the future." [24]

What they build

### A drone, a rocket, a robot, a satellite.

Each from the record: what is under contract or claimed, in the companies' own filings, calls and awards.

The drone · Anduril **Fury, an autonomous fighter**

Selected by the Air Force for production in June 2026. The first Ohio-built Fury left the line July 27, 2026; the line can build up to 150 a year. [29]

Palmer Luckey · founder

The rocket · SpaceX **National security launch**

Anticipated value $5,923,580,297 for SpaceX in the Space Force's Phase 3 Lane 2 award, Apr. 4, 2025. [16]

Elon Musk · founder

The robot · Tesla **Optimus, a humanoid**

Optimus will be the biggest product ever. Musk, July 22, 2026. His pay package counts a goal of one million robots delivered. [11][13]

Elon Musk · 19.9 percent of Tesla

The satellite · SpaceX **Starshield**

A $1.8 billion contract with the National Reconnaissance Office for a spy satellite network, signed 2021, reported by Reuters, Mar. 16, 2024. [17]

Elon Musk · founder

Two of the three co-directors founded the companies that build them.

**The factories, mapped: thirteen sites**

Anduril, Tesla, SpaceX and xAI plants in eight states, from Starbase to Redmond, named in the companies' own releases, filings and calls. Ohio is in gold.

Swipe the map →

**The robots, in Tesla's own words: a million of them, on paper**

Optimus, a general purpose, autonomous humanoid robot Tesla quarterly report, filed July 23, 2026 [12]

1 Million Bots Delivered one of the four product goals in Musk's 2025 pay package, Tesla proxy, Sept. 17, 2025 [13]

Sort of aspirationally 10 million units a year versus 1 million units a year of Optimus three. Musk, on the next version in Austin, July 22, 2026 [11]

There is no humanoid robot that is actually able to do generalized tasks. Musk, same call [11]

What the record does not say: no Tesla filing mentions military use, and no statement from Tesla, xAI or SpaceX about humanoid robots for the Department was found, for or against. In 2017 Musk signed an open letter to the United Nations, with many others, warning that Lethal autonomous weapons threaten to become the third revolution in warfare. [12][14]

Ohio · Pickaway County

### Arsenal-1, south of Columbus.

Swipe the map →

**Arsenal-1**, Anduril. Announced Jan. 16, 2025: 5 million square feet on 500 acres near Rickenbacker, more than 4,000 jobs by 2035, over $900 million in capital. First Ohio-built Fury, July 27, 2026. [26][29]

**Wright-Patterson Air Force Base**, near Dayton. Headquarters of Air Force Materiel Command and the Air Force Research Laboratory; about 38,000 people, the state's largest single-site employer. [30]

**Columbus**, the Statehouse.

**4,000+ jobs** promised by 2035, the largest jobs project in Ohio's history, per the Governor [26]

**$452.3 million** estimated value of a 2.594 percent, 30-year job creation tax credit, approved Jan. 27, 2025 [27][28]

**$310 million** JobsOhio grant over ten years, signed July 2025 [28]

**$70 million** requested from the All Ohio Future Fund at announcement [26]

The future of American air power will be made in Ohio!

**Gov. Mike DeWine** · Jan. 16, 2025 [26]

One of the three people asked what the next war will need founded the company building the largest jobs project in Ohio's history, with public incentives of more than three quarters of a billion dollars attached.

**The plant, step by step**

**March 2026:** Fury production work begins, three months ahead of the July target. [29]

**July 27, 2026:** the first Ohio-built Fury rolls off the line. [29]

**Sept. 22, 2026:** Altius 600 production added; Roadrunner and Barracuda lines hiring. [29]

The incentives are tied to Anduril meeting its job and payroll commitments over 30 years, according to the Statehouse News Bureau. A local tax abatement and a current headcount are not on the public record. [28]

The public-private shape

### A memo, a contractor, three co-directors.

- Who appointed the three? RecordThe Secretary, from the stage and in the release. The memo names only the technology officer. [3][5][6]
- Who leads the work? RecordMITRE, a nonprofit that runs federally funded research centers, in its own statement of Oct. 2. It lists 17 more participants. [7]
- Are the three federal employees for this, paid or unpaid? UnknownNot stated by the Department, MITRE or the three. In 2025 Musk served at the White House as a special government employee, which carries ethics rules. [7][32]
- Can the study buy anything or create the command? RecordNo. It proposes; the command needs a law; the money needs Congress. [5]

In reply · relayed by Politico, Oct. 2

**Sen. Mark Kelly**, D-Ariz.: Forgive me if I'm skeptical of entrusting the future of American warfare to people with zero military experience who stand to financially benefit from the decisions they're making [8]

**Sen. Jeanne Shaheen**, D-N.H., called the commission an example of Hegseth putting his political alliances ahead of our national security. [8]

**Bill Hartung**, Project on Government Oversight: Musk and Luckey should be treated as vendors. [8]

On war, in his own words

### What the Secretary told 600 junior officers and enlisted leaders.

[Image: Pete Hegseth standing on stage in front of a screen showing the American flag.]

Pete Hegseth, Secretary of War, Quantico · Official DoW photo · public domain · cropped [4]

The speech reestablished a singular mission for this department, war fighting. about 0:01, describing his 2025 address at Quantico [3]

Drone warfare supercharged by SI-enabled targeting is the biggest battlefield revolution in generations. about 21:56 [3]

We're not looking for war, but we will be prepared if one comes. about 36:44 [3]

And the historic $1.5 trillion budget that the president demands, which we will deliver, will ensure that we are equipped to win and fight every future fight. about 19:43 [3]

Lethality is your calling card and victory your only acceptable end state. about 50:51, closing [3]

The President did not speak at Quantico. His words on war that week came at the lunch gaggle on September 29, about Iran: the war to stop the nuclear weapon. On China and AI: we have to keep it that way. The Secretary's speech does not name China. [9][3]

### About two hundred yards away.

our first meeting with those three great Americans and a small group of us is happening in a skiff about 200 yards away right after this speech.

# Issue 2, in Plain Numbers · The Well · DNSC

> What Lakota's Issue 2 school bond means for your property tax bill if it passes or fails, from the public record.

Issue 2, in Plain Numbers · The Lakota school bond, from the public record

Tax year 2025 rates · Lakota Local School District · Tax district M56, West Chester Township

## What Issue 2 means for your tax bill

A local school bond on the November 3, 2026 ballot: Issue 2, Lakota Local School District, Butler County, Ohio. Type in your home and see what it means for your tax bill. Every number comes from the public record, with the source cited.

**Why this exists**

The official figures are spread across several documents: millage, abstracts, roll-offs, a plan in one PDF and a ballot line in another. This tool brings them into one place, each traced to its public source, as an example of a new kind of helpful tool for citizens.

A text field: Appraised value, starting at $350,000.

A slider sets Appraised value from 120000 to 800000, starting at 350000.

|---|---|---|---|

Your actual bill is a bit lower after state credits; the old bonds get them, and Issue 2 would not. The 2029 columns are estimates: the county sets bond rates each year, and the ballot's 2.20 mills is an average over 37 years. None of this includes the possible operating levy below, which is not on this ballot.

Source: Issue 2 ballot language and board resolution (June 9, 2026); Ohio DTE 27 tax rate abstract, tax year 2025; Lakota audited debt schedule, FY2025. Figures as of Oct 2, 2026.[6][1][2]

### What the $300.6 million plan would build

The plan costs $300.6 million. Local taxpayers would pay $223.5 million; the state would pay 33 percent of the $233.8 million co-funded work (about $77 million in the April plan; $76.7 million in the state's July approval). Grades 6 to 12 move into 4 campuses, and 21 buildings become 18.

Source: Lakota board presentation "The Plan," April 13, 2026; Ohio Facilities Construction Commission conditional approval, July 28, 2026.[8]

### Not on this ballot: a possible operating levy

The district's own forecast shows its general fund cash going negative in FY2030 without new money. It assumes a 3.6-mill operating levy from 2029. That levy is separate from Issue 2 and is not on this ballot. The treasurer's notes add that savings from the facilities plan could reduce or remove the need for it.

Source: Lakota Five-Year Forecast and its notes (including the FY2025 transfers), approved by the board Aug 24, 2026. FY2027 on are projections.[4]

#### What the district's forecast assumes

**Operating levy in the forecast.** 3.6 mills, assumed to pass in 2028 and collected from 2029.

**What it would raise.** $11.3 million in FY2029 and $21.8 million in FY2030, in the forecasts approved Feb 23 and Aug 24, 2026.

**On this home, per year.** 3.6 mills on 35 percent of the appraised value, before credits. The same whether Issue 2 passes or fails.

**Status.** On no ballot and not filed, as of Oct 2, 2026. The treasurer's notes say savings from the facilities plan could reduce or remove the need for it.

Sources: Lakota Five-Year Forecasts, approved Feb 23 and Aug 24, 2026.[4]

**Fine print: sources, timeline and method**

**The public records behind these numbers**

Verified **Ohio Division of Tax Equalization, DTE 27 Abstract of Tax Rates, tax year 2025, Butler County, Lakota LSD.** Two bond levies are on the books:[1]

| Rate | Purpose | Voted | Term | Levy authorized through |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.000 | Bond ($44,571,000) | Nov 7, 2000 | 26 yrs | tax year 2025 (collected 2026) |
| 1.280 | Bond ($84,300,000) | Nov 8, 2005 | 28 yrs | tax year 2032 |
| **2.280** | **total bond mills today** |  |  |  |

The "authorized through" year is how long the levy *may* run, not when the debt is paid. The payoff date is set by the bonds themselves, and those were refunded. The district's Sept 25, 2026 post says the same: four series totaling $34.9 million, an average 2.28 mills needed 2026 to 2028, the 2005 series paid off in 2026, the 2020 series in 2027, the 2020A series in 2028.[7]

Verified **Ohio Auditor of State, Lakota LSD audited financial statements, FY2023, debt note.** The 2005-dated series (the 2006 Refunding) matures December 1, 2026. The 2020 Refunding matures December 1, 2027. The 2013 refunding of the 2005 bonds matures December 1, 2029. The only series maturing in 2034 is the 2014 school improvement bonds.[2] Updated by the **FY2025 audit** (opinion dated Dec 26, 2025): bonds outstanding $61.58M principal at June 30, 2025; the 2006 Refunding ($9.66M) matures Dec 1, 2026; the 2020 Refunding ($13.9M) Dec 1, 2027; the 2020A and 2020B refundings ($30.9M) carry no printed maturity; a 2016 refunding runs to Dec 1, 2033. Debt service by fiscal year: FY2026 $14.44M, FY2027 $14.20M, FY2028 $14.22M, FY2029 $12.42M (the last big maturity, paid from taxes collected in 2028), FY2030 $2.09M, then about $2.0M a year through FY2035. The audit's note: bonds are paid "from the debt service and permanent improvement funds." In FY2025 the debt-service fund paid $9.47M and the permanent-improvement fund $1.81M.[2]

Unknown Whether the smaller series after 2028 are paid from the voted bond levy or from the 2-mill permanent-improvement fund. That decides whether a residual of up to about a third of a mill stays on the bill in 2029 to 2035 either way. A public-records request for the debt-service schedule by series and by fund settles it.

Verified **The county's own Levy Calculator, run on a West Chester home appraised at $322,330 (taxable $112,820), Sept 29 and again Oct 2, 2026.** It shows the Lakota bond as **Current Tax $0.00, Additional Tax $248.20**. The same parcel's Current Tax Distribution tab shows the two existing Lakota bonds at 2.28 mills, **$257.21** a year. The calculator shows only the new levy; the current bond tax is on the separate distribution tab.[3]

Verified **An operating levy is in the district's own five-year forecast**, approved by the board Feb 23, 2026 and again Aug 24, 2026: a new **3.6-mill** operating levy assumed to pass in 2028 and collect from 2029 ($11.3M in FY2029, $21.8M in FY2030). It is on no ballot. It would apply whether Issue 2 passes or fails.[4]

Verified **Issue 2 as certified by the Butler County Board of Elections and the board's June 9, 2026 resolution (5 to 0):** a bond issue of $223,483,492 over 37 years, estimated average 2.20 mills, about $77 per $100,000 of market value on a certified taxable value of $5,338,361,890, bonds dated about Feb 1, 2027 at an estimated net average interest rate of 5.00%, first collection 2029.[5][6] **Total repayment, estimated:** at the resolution's 5% estimate and level payments over 37 years, total repayment would be roughly $495 million, about $13.4 million a year, of which about $271 million is interest. That is an arithmetic estimate from the resolution's own figures, not a district number; the real schedule depends on the rates when the bonds sell.[6]

Verified **One mill in Lakota is about $5.34 million** on the taxable value the county auditor certified for the resolution ($5,338,361,890).[6] The 2026 reappraisal raised values countywide by a median of 19 percent (auditor's FAQ, June 30, 2026);[10] the district's August forecast assumes 9 percent for homes.[4] Because a bond levy raises a fixed dollar amount, higher values mean fewer mills, not more dollars.

Verified **The ballot question, as the board's June 9, 2026 resolution sets it:** "Shall bonds be issued by the Lakota Local School District... in the principal amount of $223,483,492, to be repaid annually over a maximum period of 37 years, and an annual levy of property taxes be made outside the ten-mill limitation, estimated by the county auditor to average over the repayment period of the bond issue 2.20 mills for each $1 of taxable value, which amounts to $77 for each $100,000 of the county auditor's market value, commencing in 2028, first due in calendar year 2029..."[6]

Verified **The votes (board roll calls).** May 20, 2026, resolution of necessity: passed 4 to 1. The same night an earned-income-tax alternative failed 2 to 3. June 9, 2026, resolution to proceed: passed 5 to 0.[6]

Verified **What the money builds (board deck, April 13, 2026, "The Plan").** Plains Junior addition and renovation $58.7M; East Freshman addition and renovation $55.3M; East High School campus $57.6M; West High School campus $58.3M; demolition of Ridge, Adena and Creekside/West Freshman about $3.8M; locally funded items $51.5M; permanent improvements $15.3M. Total $300.6M ($300,627,663); state share 33 percent of the $233.8M co-funded work, about $77.1M; local share $223,483,492. Grades K to 5 stay in 13 elementaries; 6 to 8 at East Freshman and Plains; 9 to 12 at East and West. Twenty-one buildings become eighteen. The state's Facilities Construction Commission gave conditional approval July 28, 2026 (Classroom Facilities Assistance Program, Segment One): state share $76,681,895, and the board must accept by Nov 25, 2026.[8]

Verified **Enrollment (FutureThink study, done at the state's request, March 11, 2026):** 17,249 students in all in 2025 to 26. On the study's projection basis (16,913, which leaves out regular preschool and full-time JVS students), enrollment peaks near 17,116 in 2029 to 30 and ends 358 lower by 2035 to 36. The district's March 26, 2026 post says the state's 2024 study had forecast about 2,000 more students over ten years; its FAQ says buildings are over capacity by more than 700 today.[9][7]

Verified **The credits are changing under state law.** The 10 percent non-business and 2.5 percent owner-occupancy credits apply only to levies approved before late 2013; the state abstract marks the 2000 and 2005 bonds as qualifying, and a new bond would not.[1][10] House Bill 186 raises the owner-occupancy credit (to as much as 15.38 percent) and phases the non-business credit down to zero over four years starting tax year 2026, on qualifying levies only. Its inflation-cap credit is $0 for the Lakota school levies, because the district's operating levies have not reached the 20-mill floor; Lakota homes may still get the Butler Tech (JVSD) portion, estimated at $12.16 per $100,000. House Bill 96's veto override (item 66, completed Oct 1, 2025) ends replacement, emergency and substitute levies for elections on or after Jan 1, 2026. This page shows the bill before credits; your treasurer's bill applies them.[10][11]

**How this bond came to be**

| When | What happened |
|---|---|
| Nov 2000 | Voters approve a $44,571,000 bond, 1.00 mill, 26 years.[1] |
| Nov 2005 | Voters approve an $84,300,000 bond, 1.28 mills, 28 years. Together the two levies are the 2.28 mills on today's bill.[1] |
| 2006 to 2020 | The district refinances those bonds several times at lower rates (refunding series including 2006, 2013, 2016, 2020, 2020A and 2020B), which is why they are paid off years before the levies' authorized end dates.[2] |
| 2024 | A state enrollment study projects about 2,000 more students over ten years. (The district's facilities planning began in 2018.)[7] |
| June 30, 2025 | Board votes 4 to 1 to place a $506,359,503 bond (4.99 mills, $175 per $100,000) and a 0.95-mill permanent-improvement levy ($33 per $100,000) on the November ballot: $208 per $100,000 as written. The district put the net change, after the old bonds end, at 2.66 mills, about $93 per $100,000.[7] |
| Nov 4, 2025 | Voters reject it as Issue 10: 60.8 percent against.[12] |
| Mar 11, 2026 | A new enrollment study (FutureThink) reverses the forecast: 17,249 students now and a projected decline of 358 by 2035 to 36. The district says buildings are over capacity by more than 700 today.[9][7] |
| Apr 13, 2026 | The board sees "The Plan": grades 6 to 12 only, four campuses, $300.6 million total, about $77 million from the state (33 percent of the co-funded work), $223.5 million local, 21 buildings to 18.[7] |
| May 20, 2026 | Resolution of necessity passes 4 to 1. An earned-income-tax alternative fails 2 to 3.[6] |
| June 9, 2026 | Resolution to proceed passes 5 to 0: $223,483,492, 37 years, estimated 2.20 mills, first collection 2029, timed to the old bonds finishing.[6] |
| July 28, 2026 | The Ohio Facilities Construction Commission gives conditional approval; state share $76.7 million; the board must accept by Nov 25, 2026.[8] |
| Aug 17, 2026 | The Board of Elections certifies it as Issue 2.[5] |
| Aug 24, 2026 | The board approves a five-year forecast that again models a 3.6-mill operating levy for 2028, and says the facilities plan's savings could reduce or remove the need for it.[4] |
| Sept 25, 2026 | The district publishes its bond roll-off schedule: four outstanding series totaling $34.9 million, with about 2.2 mills rolling off after 2028.[7] |

**How this is calculated, and how honest it is**

Ohio taxes **35 percent** of a home's appraised value. West Chester Township homes in Lakota are tax district `M56`, about **47 effective mills** on a home; Liberty Township homes in Lakota (`D20`) are about 45 because the township rate is lower, and the school lines are identical. Your bill is that rate on 35 percent of the value you set. One mill is about `$35 per $100,000`.

**Pass or fail:** Issue 2's collection begins in 2029, so it does not change today's bill. The chart compares the 2 outcomes year by year for the value you set. All figures are before credits. Issue 6 is a countywide mental-health renewal at the same rate you pay now.

**Honest about the numbers:** the district rates and ballot figures are the county's TY2025 numbers and the certified ballot; the split across bodies uses each body's effective residential rate from the county. Your treasurer's bill is always the record. Sources: Ohio DTE 27 abstract, tax year 2025; Butler County Auditor 2025 Tax Rates and Levy Calculator; Ohio Auditor of State, Lakota FY2023 and FY2025 audits; Butler County BOE certified Nov 3, 2026 issues; Lakota five-year forecast updates.

Olson](https://randalolson.com).** Figures use the county's tax year 2025 rates, the certified November 2026 ballot, the state rate abstract, and the district's audited debt schedule and five-year forecast; years marked as estimates are set each year by the county. The bill split uses the county's effective rates, before credits. Confirm any real number with the county. Last verified Oct 2, 2026. # What's in the jar · Cannabis in Ohio · DNSC

> How strong today's cannabis is, what Ohio's law allows, where the money goes, and what the research says, in plain numbers with every source linked.

What's in the jar · Cannabis in Ohio, from the public record

Ohio law as of Mar 20, 2026 · Sales through Sep 19, 2026 · Research through Aug 2026

Ohio · law, money and health

## What's in the jar.

How strong today's cannabis is, what Ohio's law allows, where the money goes, and what the research says. Plain numbers, every source a click away.

[Chart: A line drawing of a jar with a leaf inside]

1 · Then and now

### The weed in today's jar is several times stronger than it was in the 1990s.

Seized flower averaged about 4% THC in 1995. Legal flower now averages about 20%, and concentrates often run 50 to 90%.

Seized flower (DEA samples) · Seized hash oil · Legal market, Washington · Typical concentrates

[Chart: THC potency from 1995 to 2026 with Ohio's legal caps of 35 percent for flower and 70 percent for extracts]

**~4% → ~20%** Average THC in flower, 1995 seized samples to today's legal stores.

**35% cap** Ohio's limit for flower, for medical and adult use alike.

**70% cap** Ohio's limit for extracts since March 20, 2026, down from Issue 2's 90% floor.

**Sources for this part**

The DEA samples are seizures of illegal product, so they understate what legal stores sell. Labels can be off too: in a 2025 Colorado study, only 56.7% of flower products tested within 15% of their labeled THC. No public data on the average THC of products sold in Ohio exists; lab results are reported into the state's tracking system.

- ElSohly et al., [Biological Psychiatry, 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26903403/) (about 4% in 1995 to about 12% in 2014).
- Chandra et al., [Eur Arch Psychiatry Clin Neurosci, 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30671616/) (8.9% in 2008 to 17.1% in 2017; hash oil 6.7% to 55.7%).
- ElSohly et al., [Biol Psychiatry: CNNI, 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33508497/) (14.88% in 2018, 13.88% in 2019).
- Smart, Caulkins, Kilmer et al., [Addiction, 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28556310/) (Washington legal market: flower 20.6%, extracts 68.7%).
- [Int J Drug Policy, 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38043404/) (concentrates 50 to 90% THC).
- [Scientific Reports, 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40592871/) (Colorado label accuracy).
- Ohio Revised Code [3796.06(E)](https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-3796.06) and the LSC [Final Analysis of S.B. 56](https://www.legislature.ohio.gov/download?key=27450) (35% plant, 70% extract).

How much THC is in that?

A choice (Product): Flower, Dab, Vape cartridge.

A slider sets THC on the label from 1 to 90, starting at 20.

Ohio caps extracts at 70% THC. Stronger products exist in other states and in older stock.

A slider sets Amount from 0.05 to 3.5, starting at 1.

200 mg of THC in it

This counts the THC in the product; how much reaches your body depends on how it's used. Each dot is 10 mg, the most THC Canada allows in a whole package of edibles.

2 · What the law says

### Ohio said yes in 2023, then rewrote the rules in 2026.

Voters passed Issue 2 with 57%. The legislature replaced it with Senate Bill 56, which took effect March 20, 2026 and now governs medical and adult use together.

1. Sep 2016 **Medical marijuana becomes legal** House Bill 523. The first medical sales come in January 2019.
2. Nov 2023 **Issue 2 passes, 57% to 43%** Adults 21 and over can buy, carry and grow at home.
3. Aug 2024 **Adult-use sales begin** At stores licensed for both medical and adult use.
4. Jun 2025 **The budget redirects the tax money** House Bill 96 replaces Issue 2's split. More below.
5. Mar 2026 **Senate Bill 56 takes effect** One law for medical and adult use. Extract cap falls to 70%. Intoxicating hemp moves into dispensaries.
6. Dec 11, 2026 **Federal hemp rule arrives** A new national definition of hemp, delayed one month by Congress.

2.5 oz · **Possession limit** for plant material, plus 15 grams of extract.

6 / 12 · **Home grow:** 6 plants per adult, 12 per home. Going over by any number is now a crime.

0.4 mg · **Hemp limit:** more THC than this per container, and it's legally marijuana, sold only in dispensaries.

400 · **Statewide cap** on dispensaries, at least a mile apart. 231 operate today.

Home · **Smoking and vaping** are allowed only on private residential or farm property.

**The details: what changed with Senate Bill 56**

**Structure.** SB 56 repealed the Issue 2 law (Chapter 3780) and merged both markets into Chapter 3796. Licenses are now dual-use.

**Potency.** 35% THC for plant material and 70% for extracts, for medical and adult use. Issue 2 had told regulators to set limits no lower than 35% and 90%. The state may raise the extract limit by rule. A Division of Cannabis Control guidance sheet dated March 2026 still lists 90% for manufactured products, so confirm with the Division before relying on one number.

**Hemp.** Since March 20, 2026, hemp means no more than 0.3% total THC, including THCA. A finished product with more than 0.4 mg of THC per container, or with cannabinoids made outside the plant (such as delta-8 converted from CBD), is not hemp. A plan to let bars and stores sell hemp drinks was vetoed. A federal court has blocked parts of the ban for ten plaintiff companies; the appeal is pending.

**Other changes.** Marijuana bought out of state is contraband. No new dispensary within a mile of another, or where liquor is sold. Stricter packaging and advertising. A path to expunge past minor possession offenses. Local governments can ban new operators but not home grow, and can't close stores licensed before March 20, 2026.

**Tax.** The 10% rate stayed. An earlier version of SB 56 would have raised it to 15%.

- Ohio Legislative Service Commission, [Final Analysis of S.B. 56](https://www.legislature.ohio.gov/download?key=27450) (corrected Apr 2, 2026) and [bill status](https://www.legislature.ohio.gov/legislation/136/sb56).
- Ohio Revised Code [3796.06](https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-3796.06), [3796.01](https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-3796.01), [3796.40](https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-3796.40).
- Division of Cannabis Control, [Total THC Content Guidance](https://dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/com.ohio.gov/DCC/Total_THC_Content_Guidance.pdf) (03/2026).
- Issue 2 results (57.19% yes): [Wikipedia, citing the Ohio Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Ohio_Issue_2).
- Federal hemp: Congressional Research Service, [LSB11381](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-12-08_LSB11381_8b411fbfb79325154a586ad1fbba21298039afe5.html); the Dec 11, 2026 delay as reported by [Akerman](https://www.akerman.com/en/perspectives/congress-approves-one-month-delay-of-federal-hemp-thc-restrictions.html).
- Hemp litigation: [KMK Law, Aug 2026](https://www.kmklaw.com/cannabis-and-craft-beer/ohio-hemp-ban-stalled-federal-court-sides-with-hemp-industry).

3 · Where the money goes

### By September, adult-use sales had already passed all of 2025.

Ohioans have bought $4.3 billion of legal cannabis since 2019. As adult use grew, the medical program shrank by more than half.

Adult use · Medical · 2026 runs through Sept 19

[Chart: Ohio legal cannabis sales by year, 2019 to 2026, adult use and medical]

**$844M** Adult-use sales in 2026 through Sept 19, versus about $830M in all of 2025.

**10% + sales tax** On adult use. In Butler County the sales tax adds about 6.5%.

**−59%** Active medical patients, from 178,703 in Oct 2023 to 72,943 in Jul 2026.

The 10% tax, under Issue 2

Equity 36% · Host towns 36% · Addiction 25%

Social equity and jobs 36%, host communities 36%, addiction services 25%, administration 3%.

Since June 30, 2025

State general fund 64% · Host towns 36%

The state budget ended the equity and addiction shares. Host money goes to each town with a dispensary, for any lawful purpose.

Butler County

**Monroe** 4 dispensaries · about $886,000 in the first host payment

**Seven Mile** 1 dispensary · about $401,000 in the first host payment

**Oxford** 2 dispensaries, the most the city allows

**Fairfield** 1 dispensary, licensed June 2026

**Middletown** 1 or 2 dispensaries

**Hamilton** Ban reported lifted July 2026; none licensed yet

**West Chester Twp** Moratorium still in place

**Liberty Twp** Moratorium still in place

**Sources and notes for this part**

Yearly sales are the change in the state's cumulative weekly totals. 2026 runs through the week ending Sept 19. Depending on where the year's weeks are cut, 2025 adult use was $829M or $836M; the chart uses the calendar-week cut for both markets. The state's Oct 2 summary sheet repeats the adult-use figures in its medical and total columns, so this page uses the weekly spreadsheet. Statewide tax collected isn't published in a primary source; 10% of adult-use sales since launch would be roughly $192 million, an estimate, not an official figure. Host payments are from the first distribution on Jan 7, 2026, as reported by the Journal-News. Butler County dispensaries were matched to the state list by address and are approximate. Statewide, an Ohio State law school tracker counts 224 places with moratoriums as of Oct 1, 2026, and says the list may be incomplete.

- Division of Cannabis Control, [Historical Sales Data](https://dam.assets.ohio.gov/raw/upload/com.ohio.gov/DCC/DCC%20Stats/NEW_-_DCC_Historical_Sales_Data.xlsx) (weekly, through Sep 19, 2026) and [Program Update: By the Numbers](https://dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/com.ohio.gov/DCC/DCC%20Stats/DCC_Update_By_The_Numbers.pdf) (Oct 2, 2026; licensees and patients).
- Ohio Revised Code [3796.40](https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-3796.40) (10% tax, 64/36 split); [former 3780.23](https://codes.ohio.gov/assets/laws/revised-code/authenticated/37/3780/3780.23/12-7-2023/3780.23-12-7-2023.pdf) (Issue 2 split); [3780.22 as amended by H.B. 96](https://codes.ohio.gov/assets/laws/revised-code/authenticated/37/3780/3780.22/6-30-2025/3780.22-6-30-2025.pdf).
- Journal-News / Dayton Daily News, [first host-community payments](https://www.daytondailynews.com/local/area-communities-finally-getting-millions-in-cannabis-tax-revenue/7I4DOBLIRRG2RPFV4I3ITWVQHA/), Jan 2026.
- Division of Cannabis Control, [dispensary list](https://com.ohio.gov/divisions-and-programs/cannabis-control/about-dcc/licenses/dispensaries/dispensary-licenses) and [map](https://com.ohio.gov/divisions-and-programs/cannabis-control/about-dcc/licenses/what-we-do/cannabis-dispensary-map).
- Ohio State Moritz College of Law, [Ohio marijuana moratoriums](https://moritzlaw.osu.edu/research/local-moratoriums-ohio-adult-use-marijuana-operators); FOX19, [Hamilton lifts its ban](https://www.fox19.com/2026/07/16/hamilton-city-council-votes-lift-ban-marijuana-dispensaries/), Jul 16, 2026; [West Chester moratorium](https://www.wcpo.com/news/local-news/butler-county/west-chester/west-chester-twp-extends-moratorium-on-recreational-marijuana-businesses) (WCPO).
- Sales tax rates: [Butler County](https://www.salestaxhandbook.com/ohio/rates/butler).

4 · What the research says

### The clearest risk is daily use of high-potency cannabis, especially for the young.

The strongest studies find more psychosis among people who use strong cannabis every day. Some of the link also runs the other way, so read these as associations.

Odds of a first psychotic episode, compared with people who never used

Never used

**1×**

Daily use, any cannabis

**3.2×**

Daily use, high-potency (THC 10% or more)

**4.8×**

Di Forti et al., Lancet Psychiatry, 2019: 901 first-episode patients and 1,237 controls at 11 sites in Europe and Brazil. Gridlines every 1×.

**"Substantial"** The National Academies' word for the evidence linking cannabis and schizophrenia, highest among the most frequent users.

**15%** Share of schizophrenia among Danish men 16 to 49 that could be tied to cannabis use disorder in 2021, if the link is causal.

**11×** Risk of a psychotic disorder for teens who used cannabis in an Ontario study. No significant link for young adults.

**The arrow points both ways.** A genetic study found only a small causal effect of starting cannabis on schizophrenia, and stronger evidence that people predisposed to schizophrenia are more likely to use cannabis. Most "cases that could be prevented" figures assume the link is causal. People with a family history of psychosis show more sensitivity to cannabis, but no study has measured risk by product strength for them.

**More findings: dependence, withdrawal, vomiting, daily use**

**Potency and dependence.** A review of 20 studies found higher-potency use was linked to more psychosis and more cannabis use disorder; results for depression and anxiety were mixed.

**Tolerance.** In a Colorado study, people using concentrates had more than twice the THC in their blood as flower users but no more measured impairment, consistent with tolerance. That is not evidence that concentrates are harmless. Dab users report more tolerance and withdrawal.

**Withdrawal.** About 47% of regular or dependent users have cannabis withdrawal, from 17% in general surveys to 87% among inpatients.

**Severe vomiting (cannabis hyperemesis syndrome).** U.S. emergency visits coded for it rose sharply after a dedicated diagnosis code began in October 2025; the CDC says better coding may explain part of the jump. In Ontario, visits rose 13-fold from 2014 to 2021.

**Daily use.** In 2025, 21.4 million Americans used marijuana on 20 or more days in the past month, more than the 17.2 million who drank that often. In Ohio, 16% of people 12 and older used marijuana in the past month (2023 to 2024), and 28% of those 18 to 25.

- National Academies, [The Health Effects of Cannabis and Cannabinoids](https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/24625/chapter/2), 2017.
- Di Forti et al., [Lancet Psychiatry, 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30902669/).
- Hjorthøj et al., [Psychological Medicine, 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37140715/).
- McDonald et al., [Psychological Medicine, 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38775165/) (Ontario, ages 12 to 24).
- Gage et al., [Psychological Medicine, 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27928975/) (Mendelian randomization).
- GROUP Investigators, [Archives of General Psychiatry, 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20921112/) (siblings).
- Petrilli et al., [Lancet Psychiatry, 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35901795/); Bidwell et al., [JAMA Psychiatry, 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32520316/); Loflin & Earleywine, [Addictive Behaviors, 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24930049/); Bahji et al., [JAMA Network Open, 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32271390/).
- CDC, [MMWR, Aug 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42560855/); Myran et al., [JAMA Network Open, 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36112372/).
- SAMHSA, [2025 NSDUH detailed tables](https://www.samhsa.gov/data/report/2025-nsduh-detailed-tables) and [2023–2024 state estimates](https://www.samhsa.gov/data/sites/default/files/reports/rpt56986/2024-nsduh-sae-state-tabs1/2024-nsduh-sae-state-tabs.htm).

5 · What other places tried

### Caps, potency taxes and small edibles. No one has measured the health results yet.

Ohio's caps are higher than Vermont's and Quebec's. Here is what other places did.

Ohio **35% · 70%** Flower and extract caps, the same for medical and adult use.

Vermont **30% · 60%** Flower and solid concentrates. Its own cannabis board called the evidence for the concentrate cap inconclusive.

Illinois **10% → 25%** A potency-tiered tax: 10% on flower up to 35% THC, 25% above it.

Canada **10 mg** The most THC allowed in a whole package of edibles. A 2024 review kept it and suggested taxes that rise with THC.

Quebec **30%** A cap on non-edible products. A 2026 study found less use of strong extracts, and more illegal buying. It can't isolate the cap's effect.

No real-world evaluation of how U.S. potency caps or potency taxes affect health exists yet.

**The tradeoff, and sources**

Caps and steep potency taxes may cut exposure to the strongest legal products, and they may push some buyers to illegal or out-of-state sellers. In a 2026 experiment with 1,525 U.S. buyers, potency-based taxes moved people away from the strongest products but didn't lower total THC use, and up to 89% of that shift could be offset by buying illegally. Massachusetts regulators found the evidence insufficient to recommend a cap in 2021, while noting greater risk for young people using high-THC products. RAND has proposed taxing THC content directly.

- Vermont, [7 V.S.A. § 868](https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/07/033/00868); Vermont Cannabis Control Board, [concentrates report](https://ccb.vermont.gov/sites/ccb/files/2022-12/Final%20draft%20-%20VT%20Concentrates%20report%20-1.pdf), Dec 2022.
- Illinois Department of Revenue, [cannabis excise rates](https://tax.illinois.gov/research/taxrates/excise).
- Health Canada, [Cannabis Act review, expert panel final report](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/publications/drugs-medication/legislative-review-cannabis-act-final-report-expert-panel.html), Mar 2024.
- [Canadian Journal of Public Health, 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42032371/) (Quebec).
- He et al., [Health Economics, 2026](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13508039/).
- RAND, [Promises and Pitfalls of Cannabis Taxes](https://www.rand.org/pubs/commentary/2016/08/promises-and-pitfalls-of-cannabis-taxes.html), 2016.

# The River · The Well · DNSC

> Name what you are carrying, set it on a leaf, and watch the water take it. Nothing is stored or sent.

The Well · Letting go

## The River

Name what you are carrying, set it on a leaf, and watch the water take it.

Just the thing itself, in a few words: a worry, a grief, a grudge, a fear.

A text box: What are you carrying? Name it plainly. (Something you're carrying right now).

Enter sets it on the water

A button: Set it on the water.

Just watch. Breathe in for 4, hold for 2, out for 6.

Gone downstream.

A text box: What is left, now that it's moving? (Whatever remains, if anything).

This one is yours to skip

Buttons: Leave, Set this on the water too.

Only time and practice move things. Come back when you need the water.

[Leave when you're ready →](https://tools.dnsc.ai/well/)

**The four moves**

1. **Name it.** Say the thing plainly, in a few words.
2. **Watch it.** Set it outside yourself and let your eyes follow it. You are the river; it is the leaf.
3. **Let it pass.** It dissolves downstream. Notice what is left.
4. **Return.** Come back to the room, and to the water whenever you need it.

One pass takes about a minute. Practiced over time, it loosens the grip.

**Where this practice comes from**

**Tashlich.** On Rosh Hashanah, Jews walk to living water, a river or the sea, and cast crumbs or empty their pockets as a sign of sins carried away. The practice draws on Micah 7:19, and it has been recorded since at least the 15th century, in the customs of Rabbi Jacob Moelin (the Maharil) of the Rhineland.

**Nagashi-bina and tōrō nagashi.** In Japan, paper dolls are set afloat on rivers in early spring to carry misfortune away, a custom rooted in Shinto purification (harae). At the close of Obon, floating lanterns are set on the water to see off the spirits of the dead.

**Leaves on a stream.** A cognitive defusion exercise from Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, developed by Steven C. Hayes and colleagues from the 1980s and in print by 1999. You picture a stream, place each thought on a leaf as it comes, and watch it float by without arguing with it.

**Expressive writing.** James W. Pennebaker's studies, from 1986 onward, asked people to write plainly about what weighed on them for a few minutes on a few days. Across many studies since, that small practice has shown modest, measurable benefits to health and mood.

From each we took one move: name it, set it outside yourself, watch it move, honor it, let it pass, return.

Nothing you write here is saved or sent. It lives on the leaf until the water takes it, and then it's gone. No history, no count. Stay as long as you like, or [leave when you're ready →](https://tools.dnsc.ai/well/)

---

Source: https://tools.dnsc.ai/well/river/ · Generated from the page on Oct 4, 2026
